claim: GTPBP2 and GTPBP1 share 37% identical amino acids in their N-terminus regions.
source: Domain structure of mouse GTPBP2 and GTPBP1. The percent of identical amino acids for each domain is shown.
evidence: Figure 1A shows domain structure comparison with percentage identity values displayed for each domain

claim: GTPBP2 and GTPBP1 share approximately 60% identical amino acids in their GTP-binding domain.
source: Domain structure of mouse GTPBP2 and GTPBP1. The percent of identical amino acids for each domain is shown.
evidence: Figure 1A displays domain comparison showing ~60% identity in the GTP-binding domain

claim: GTPBP2 and GTPBP1 share 49% identical amino acids in Domain II.
source: Domain structure of mouse GTPBP2 and GTPBP1. The percent of identical amino acids for each domain is shown.
evidence: Figure 1A shows domain structure with percentage identity labeled for Domain II

claim: GTPBP2 and GTPBP1 share 51% identical amino acids in Domain III.
source: Domain structure of mouse GTPBP2 and GTPBP1. The percent of identical amino acids for each domain is shown.
evidence: Figure 1A displays domain comparison showing 51% identity in Domain III

claim: Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 are widely expressed throughout the P28 wild type cerebellum.
source: In situ hybridization demonstrating ubiquitous expression of Gtpbp1 (yellow) and Gtpbp2 (red) in the P28 wild type (B6J) cerebellum (B), and CA1 region of the hippocampus (C), dentate gyrus (DG) (D) (n = 2 mice).
evidence: In situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1B demonstrates expression patterns in cerebellar tissue

claim: Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 are expressed in the CA1 region of the hippocampus at P28.
source: In situ hybridization demonstrating ubiquitous expression of Gtpbp1 (yellow) and Gtpbp2 (red) in the P28 wild type (B6J) cerebellum (B), and CA1 region of the hippocampus (C), dentate gyrus (DG) (D) (n = 2 mice).
evidence: Figure 1C shows in situ hybridization results for CA1 hippocampal region

claim: Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 are expressed in the dentate gyrus at P28.
source: In situ hybridization demonstrating ubiquitous expression of Gtpbp1 (yellow) and Gtpbp2 (red) in the P28 wild type (B6J) cerebellum (B), and CA1 region of the hippocampus (C), dentate gyrus (DG) (D) (n = 2 mice).
evidence: Figure 1D displays in situ hybridization data for dentate gyrus

claim: Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 are ubiquitously expressed throughout the cortex at P28.
source: In situ hybridization was performed on P28 B6J mice demonstrating ubiquitous expression of Gtpbp1 (yellow) and Gtpbp2 (red) throughout the cortex (A) and specifically in layer IV (B) (n = 2 mice).
evidence: Figure 1—figure supplement 1A shows in situ hybridization results across cortical layers

claim: Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 are specifically expressed in cortical layer IV at P28.
source: In situ hybridization was performed on P28 B6J mice demonstrating ubiquitous expression of Gtpbp1 (yellow) and Gtpbp2 (red) throughout the cortex (A) and specifically in layer IV (B) (n = 2 mice).
evidence: Figure 1—figure supplement 1B shows specific expression in layer IV of the cortex

claim: Expression of Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 occurs both in neurons that degenerate in Gtpbp2-/- mice and those that do not.
source: Interestingly, expression of Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 occurred both in neurons that degenerate in Gtpbp2-/- mice (e.g. cerebellar granule cells, dentate gyrus (DG) granule cells, neurons in cortical layer IV) and those that do not (e.g. hippocampal pyramidal cells and non-layer IV cortical neurons) suggesting possible functional redundancy between these genes in some cell types.
evidence: Expression patterns observed in multiple brain regions with differential vulnerability to degeneration

claim: The expression pattern of Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 suggests possible functional redundancy between these genes in some cell types.
source: Interestingly, expression of Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 occurred both in neurons that degenerate in Gtpbp2-/- mice (e.g. cerebellar granule cells, dentate gyrus (DG) granule cells, neurons in cortical layer IV) and those that do not (e.g. hippocampal pyramidal cells and non-layer IV cortical neurons) suggesting possible functional redundancy between these genes in some cell types.
evidence: Inference based on overlapping expression patterns in neurons with different vulnerability

claim: Mice homozygous for a null mutation in Gtpbp1 on a mixed genetic background were reported to have no apparent phenotypes.
source: However, mice homozygous for a null mutation in Gtpbp1, which encodes a structurally related trGTPase (Figure 1A), were reported to have no apparent phenotypes on a mixed genetic background (Senju et al., 2000).
evidence: Citation to previous published work by Senju et al., 2000

claim: B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice were indistinguishable from littermate controls at 3 weeks of age.
source: Like B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice, B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice were indistinguishable from littermate controls at 3 weeks of age, developed overt ataxia by 6 weeks, and died by 8 weeks of age.
evidence: Observational data comparing mutant mice to controls at specific time points

claim: B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice developed overt ataxia by 6 weeks of age.
source: Like B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice, B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice were indistinguishable from littermate controls at 3 weeks of age, developed overt ataxia by 6 weeks, and died by 8 weeks of age.
evidence: Observational data on behavioral phenotype at 6 weeks

claim: B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice died by 8 weeks of age.
source: Like B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice, B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice were indistinguishable from littermate controls at 3 weeks of age, developed overt ataxia by 6 weeks, and died by 8 weeks of age.
evidence: Survival data showing lethality by 8 weeks

claim: Cerebellar degeneration in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice was similar to that observed in B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice.
source: Cerebellar degeneration was also similar to that observed in B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice (Ishimura et al., 2014; Figure 1E).
evidence: Histological comparison shown in Figure 1E and reference to previous publication

claim: Apoptotic granule cells were observed in caudal lobes of the cerebellum just prior to 4 weeks of age in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: Apoptotic granule cells were observed in caudal lobes of the cerebellum just prior to 4 weeks of age and these neurons progressively died in a posterior to anterior manner.
evidence: Temporal and spatial characterization of cell death in cerebellar tissue

claim: Cerebellar granule cells in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice progressively died in a posterior to anterior manner.
source: Apoptotic granule cells were observed in caudal lobes of the cerebellum just prior to 4 weeks of age and these neurons progressively died in a posterior to anterior manner.
evidence: Spatial progression pattern of neurodegeneration observed over time

claim: Granule cells in the dentate gyrus degenerated in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: As previously observed in B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice, granule cells in the DG, layer IV cortical neurons and multiple neurons in the retina degenerated in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice, but cell death was not observed for other neurons such as hippocampal pyramidal cells or neurons in the other layers of the cortex (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–E).
evidence: Histological analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: Layer IV cortical neurons degenerated in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: As previously observed in B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice, granule cells in the DG, layer IV cortical neurons and multiple neurons in the retina degenerated in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice, but cell death was not observed for other neurons such as hippocampal pyramidal cells or neurons in the other layers of the cortex (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–E).
evidence: Histological data showing selective neuronal death in layer IV

claim: Multiple neurons in the retina degenerated in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: As previously observed in B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice, granule cells in the DG, layer IV cortical neurons and multiple neurons in the retina degenerated in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice, but cell death was not observed for other neurons such as hippocampal pyramidal cells or neurons in the other layers of the cortex (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–E).
evidence: Retinal histology shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E

claim: Cell death was not observed for hippocampal pyramidal cells in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: As previously observed in B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice, granule cells in the DG, layer IV cortical neurons and multiple neurons in the retina degenerated in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice, but cell death was not observed for other neurons such as hippocampal pyramidal cells or neurons in the other layers of the cortex (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–E).
evidence: Absence of cell death observed in hippocampal pyramidal cells through histological analysis

claim: Cell death was not observed for neurons in non-layer IV cortical layers in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: As previously observed in B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice, granule cells in the DG, layer IV cortical neurons and multiple neurons in the retina degenerated in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice, but cell death was not observed for other neurons such as hippocampal pyramidal cells or neurons in the other layers of the cortex (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–E).
evidence: Selective vulnerability shown by absence of degeneration in other cortical layers

claim: Transgenic expression of wild type n-Tr20 greatly attenuated degeneration of cerebellar granule cells in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: Consistent with the dependency of cerebellar granule cell degeneration on levels of n-Tr20, a tRNAArgUCU gene with a processing mutation in the B6J strain, transgenic expression of wild type n-Tr20 greatly attenuated degeneration of these neurons as has previously been observed for B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice (Figure 1E).
evidence: Genetic rescue experiment shown in Figure 1E demonstrating attenuation of neurodegeneration

claim: Cerebellar granule cell degeneration in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice is dependent on levels of n-Tr20.
source: Consistent with the dependency of cerebellar granule cell degeneration on levels of n-Tr20, a tRNAArgUCU gene with a processing mutation in the B6J strain, transgenic expression of wild type n-Tr20 greatly attenuated degeneration of these neurons as has previously been observed for B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice (Figure 1E).
evidence: Genetic rescue experiment demonstrates dependency on n-Tr20 levels

claim: n-Tr20 is a tRNAArgUCU gene with a processing mutation in the B6J strain.
source: Consistent with the dependency of cerebellar granule cell degeneration on levels of n-Tr20, a tRNAArgUCU gene with a processing mutation in the B6J strain, transgenic expression of wild type n-Tr20 greatly attenuated degeneration of these neurons as has previously been observed for B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice (Figure 1E).
evidence: Description of the genetic mutation present in the B6J strain

claim: Neurodegeneration was not observed in mice heterozygous for mutations in both Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2.
source: Neurodegeneration was not observed in mice heterozygous for mutations in both Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 (Figure 1F).
evidence: Histological analysis of double heterozygous mice shown in Figure 1F

claim: The onset, progression and specificity of neurodegeneration were similar between B6J.Gtpbp1-/-; Gtpbp2-/-, B6J.Gtpbp1-/- and B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice.
source: Furthermore, the onset, progression and specificity of neurodegeneration were similar between B6J.Gtpbp1-/-; Gtpbp2-/-, B6J.Gtpbp1-/- and B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice (Figure 1F–H).
evidence: Comparative analysis of neurodegeneration patterns shown in Figure 1F-H

claim: Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 are functionally distinct and act in a common pathway to mediate cellular homeostasis necessary for neuron survival.
source: These results suggest that Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 are functionally distinct and act in a common pathway to mediate cellular homeostasis that is necessary for neuron survival.
evidence: Inference from genetic interaction studies showing non-redundant but pathway-related functions

claim: Approximately 50% of pausing genes were shared between libraries generated from individual B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: Comparison of genes with AGA pauses revealed that approximately 50% of pausing genes were shared between libraries generated from individual B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice, and this was also true for B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice, supporting that AGA pausing is likely stochastic (Figure 2C).
evidence: Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 2C demonstrating overlap between biological replicates

claim: AGA pausing is likely stochastic.
source: Comparison of genes with AGA pauses revealed that approximately 50% of pausing genes were shared between libraries generated from individual B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice, and this was also true for B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice, supporting that AGA pausing is likely stochastic (Figure 2C).
evidence: Inference from the partial overlap of pausing genes between biological replicates

claim: About 50% of genes with AGA pausing intersected between B6J.Gtpbp1-/- and B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice.
source: Similarly, about 50% of genes with AGA pausing intersected between B6J.Gtpbp1-/- and B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Venn diagram shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B comparing pausing genes between genotypes

claim: Gene ontology analysis of genes with pauses revealed enrichment in numerous biological processes.
source: Consistent with stochastic pausing at AGA codons, gene ontology (GO) analysis of genes with pauses revealed enrichment in numerous biological processes and the majority of these processes were enriched in both Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: GO analysis results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C

claim: The majority of biological processes enriched in genes with pauses were enriched in both Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 mutants.
source: Consistent with stochastic pausing at AGA codons, gene ontology (GO) analysis of genes with pauses revealed enrichment in numerous biological processes and the majority of these processes were enriched in both Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: GO analysis comparison shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C

claim: Both GTPBP1 and GTPBP2 rescue stochastic ribosome-pausing events when the tRNAArgUCU pool is reduced.
source: Thus, our data suggest that both GTPBP1 and GTPBP2 rescue stochastic ribosome-pausing events when the tRNAArgUCU pool is reduced.
evidence: Inference from ribosome profiling data showing AGA codon-specific pausing in both mutants

claim: Approximately 12% of detected genes showed significant differential expression in the cerebellum of 3-week-old B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice compared to B6J mice.
source: Comparison of data from the cerebellum of 3-week-old B6J.Gtpbp1-/- and B6J mice revealed significant (q-value ≤0.05) differential expression (DE) of approximately 12% of the detected genes, with 46% upregulated and 54% downregulated (DE Gtpbp1, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: RNA-sequencing analysis with statistical testing (q-value ≤0.05)

claim: 46% of differentially expressed genes were upregulated in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- cerebellum compared to B6J.
source: Comparison of data from the cerebellum of 3-week-old B6J.Gtpbp1-/- and B6J mice revealed significant (q-value ≤0.05) differential expression (DE) of approximately 12% of the detected genes, with 46% upregulated and 54% downregulated (DE Gtpbp1, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: RNA-seq differential expression analysis results

claim: 54% of differentially expressed genes were downregulated in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- cerebellum compared to B6J.
source: Comparison of data from the cerebellum of 3-week-old B6J.Gtpbp1-/- and B6J mice revealed significant (q-value ≤0.05) differential expression (DE) of approximately 12% of the detected genes, with 46% upregulated and 54% downregulated (DE Gtpbp1, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: RNA-seq differential expression analysis results

claim: Loss of Gtpbp2 altered expression of about 10% of detected genes in the cerebellum compared to B6J.
source: Similarly, loss of Gtpbp2 altered expression of about 10% of the detected genes with 45% and 55% upregulated and downregulated, respectively, when compared to B6J (DE Gtpbp2, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: RNA-seq differential expression analysis for Gtpbp2 mutant

claim: Only 27 genes (mostly non-coding genes) were differentially expressed between Gtpbp1-/- and Gtpbp2-/- cerebella.
source: Interestingly, only 27 genes (mostly non-coding genes) were differentially expressed between Gtpbp1-/- and Gtpbp2-/- cerebella, revealing that loss of either gene similarly altered the transcriptome (Figure 2D, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Comparative RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2D

claim: Loss of Gtpbp1 or Gtpbp2 similarly altered the transcriptome.
source: Interestingly, only 27 genes (mostly non-coding genes) were differentially expressed between Gtpbp1-/- and Gtpbp2-/- cerebella, revealing that loss of either gene similarly altered the transcriptome (Figure 2D, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Inference from the minimal differences between the two mutant transcriptomes

claim: Transcriptional alterations might reflect a common cellular response to ribosome pausing rather than changes in levels of specific genes that harbor paused ribosomes.
source: The high similarity of gene expression changes in Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 mutant mice, combined with our observation that ribosome-pausing defects are likely stochastic, suggested that transcriptional alterations might reflect a common cellular response to ribosome pausing rather than changes in levels of the specific genes that harbor paused ribosomes.
evidence: Inference from the similarity of transcriptional changes and stochastic nature of pausing

claim: Transcriptional changes were only weakly correlated with genes showing increased ribosomal occupancy (Spearman correlation coefficient of 0.0405, p-value=0.0083).
source: In agreement, transcriptional changes were only weakly correlated with genes showing increased ribosomal occupancy (Spearman correlation coefficient of 0.0405, p-value=0.0083).
evidence: Statistical correlation analysis between transcriptional changes and ribosome occupancy

claim: Significant changes in expression were only observed in 33% of genes with AGA pauses in the Gtpbp1-/- cerebellum.
source: Significant (q-value ≤0.05) changes in expression were only observed in 33% or 26% of the genes with AGA pauses (that were detected in at least two replicates) in the Gtpbp1-/- and Gtpbp2-/- cerebellum, respectively (Figure 2E).
evidence: Analysis of overlap between pausing genes and differentially expressed genes shown in Figure 2E

claim: Significant changes in expression were only observed in 26% of genes with AGA pauses in the Gtpbp2-/- cerebellum.
source: Significant (q-value ≤0.05) changes in expression were only observed in 33% or 26% of the genes with AGA pauses (that were detected in at least two replicates) in the Gtpbp1-/- and Gtpbp2-/- cerebellum, respectively (Figure 2E).
evidence: Analysis of overlap between pausing genes and differentially expressed genes

claim: Upstream regulator analysis revealed significant enrichment for activation of the transcription factor ATF4 in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: In order to identify molecular pathways that might respond to ribosome pausing, we performed upstream regulator analysis (Ingenuity Pathway Analysis) of genes differentially expressed between B6J and B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice (DE Gtpbp1). This analysis revealed significant enrichment for activation of the transcription factor ATF4, an effector of the ISR (Figure 3A, inset).
evidence: Ingenuity Pathway Analysis results shown in Figure 3A inset

claim: ATF4 is an effector of the integrated stress response (ISR).
source: This analysis revealed significant enrichment for activation of the transcription factor ATF4, an effector of the ISR (Figure 3A, inset).
evidence: Established knowledge about ATF4's role in the ISR pathway

claim: The ISR is induced by coupling of stress signals to phosphorylation of serine 51 of eIF2α to decrease translation initiation.
source: The ISR is induced by the coupling of stress signals to the phosphorylation of serine 51 of the translation initiation factor eIF2α to decrease translation initiation.
evidence: Established mechanism of ISR activation

claim: The ISR reduces translation of many mRNAs while enhancing translation of ATF4.
source: While the ISR reduces translation of many mRNAs, translation of ATF4 is enhanced, which results in the upregulation of genes to restore cellular homeostasis.
evidence: Established mechanism of selective translation during ISR

claim: Atf4 and 141 of 153 differentially expressed ATF4 target genes were upregulated in the cerebellum of 3-week-old B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: In agreement, Atf4 and 141 of the 153 differentially expressed ATF4 target genes (Han et al., 2013) were upregulated in the cerebellum of 3-week-old B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice (DE Gtpbp1, Figure 3A).
evidence: RNA-seq data analysis showing upregulation of ATF4 targets, displayed in Figure 3A

claim: Levels of phosphorylated eIF2α (p-eIF2αS51) were increased in the cerebellum of B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: Furthermore, levels of phosphorylated eIF2α (p-eIF2αS51) were increased in the cerebellum and hippocampus of B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: Western blot analysis shown in Figure 3B and quantification in Figure 3C

claim: Levels of phosphorylated eIF2α (p-eIF2αS51) were increased in the hippocampus of B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: Furthermore, levels of phosphorylated eIF2α (p-eIF2αS51) were increased in the cerebellum and hippocampus of B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: Western blot analysis shown in Figure 3B and quantification in Figure 3C

claim: ATF4 target genes were induced in hippocampal neurons of 3-week-old B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: In agreement, in situ hybridization of the B6J.Gtpbp1-/- hippocampus with probes to ATF4 targets induced in the cerebellum of these mice demonstrated that these ATF4 targets were also induced in hippocampal neurons of 3-week-old mutant mice (Figure 3D).
evidence: In situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3D

claim: Induction of ATF4 targets varied in different types of neurons.
source: Interestingly, induction of ATF4 targets varied in different types of neurons. Sesn2, Slc7a1, and Chac1 were upregulated in both CA1 and DG neurons, whereas Ddr2 was only upregulated in CA1 neurons (Figure 3D).
evidence: In situ hybridization showing differential expression patterns in Figure 3D

claim: Sesn2, Slc7a1, and Chac1 were upregulated in both CA1 and DG neurons in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: Sesn2, Slc7a1, and Chac1 were upregulated in both CA1 and DG neurons, whereas Ddr2 was only upregulated in CA1 neurons (Figure 3D).
evidence: In situ hybridization results shown in Figure 3D

claim: Ddr2 was only upregulated in CA1 neurons in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: Sesn2, Slc7a1, and Chac1 were upregulated in both CA1 and DG neurons, whereas Ddr2 was only upregulated in CA1 neurons (Figure 3D).
evidence: In situ hybridization showing CA1-specific expression in Figure 3D

claim: The ISR is activated by the eIF2α kinase GCN2 in B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice.
source: In B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice, the ISR is activated by the eIF2α kinase GCN2 (EIF2AK4).
evidence: Reference to previous findings about GCN2-mediated ISR activation

claim: Inhibition of ISR activation via Gcn2 deletion in B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice accelerated cerebellar granule cell death.
source: Inhibition of ISR activation via Gcn2 deletion in these mice accelerated cerebellar granule cell death and induced neurodegeneration of hippocampal pyramidal cells (Ishimura et al., 2016).
evidence: Citation to previous work by Ishimura et al., 2016

claim: Inhibition of ISR activation via Gcn2 deletion in B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice induced neurodegeneration of hippocampal pyramidal cells.
source: Inhibition of ISR activation via Gcn2 deletion in these mice accelerated cerebellar granule cell death and induced neurodegeneration of hippocampal pyramidal cells (Ishimura et al., 2016).
evidence: Citation to previous work by Ishimura et al., 2016

claim: GCN2 was enriched in upstream regulator analysis of differentially expressed genes in the B6J.Gtpbp1-/- cerebellum.
source: GCN2 was enriched in upstream regulator analysis of differentially expressed genes in the B6J.Gtpbp1-/- cerebellum (DE Gtpbp1), suggesting that this kinase may also mediate activation of the ISR in Gtpbp1-deficient mice (Figure 3A, inset).
evidence: Ingenuity Pathway Analysis results shown in Figure 3A inset

claim: Gcn2 deletion in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice accelerated degeneration of cerebellar granule cells.
source: In agreement, Gcn2 deletion in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice accelerated degeneration of cerebellar granule cells. In 5-week-old B6J.Gtpbp1-/-; Gcn2-/- mice, 65% of these neurons had degenerated compared to 37% in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: Histological quantification shown in Figure 3E and 3F

claim: In 5-week-old B6J.Gtpbp1-/-; Gcn2-/- mice, 65% of cerebellar granule cells had degenerated compared to 37% in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: In 5-week-old B6J.Gtpbp1-/-; Gcn2-/- mice, 65% of these neurons had degenerated compared to 37% in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: Quantitative histological analysis shown in Figure 3F

claim: The DG of B6J.Gtpbp1-/-; Gcn2-/- mice had twice the number of granule cells with pyknotic nuclei compared to B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: Furthermore, the DG of B6J.Gtpbp1-/-; Gcn2-/- mice had twice the number of granule cells with pyknotic nuclei compared to B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice (Figure 3G, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Quantification of pyknotic cells shown in Figure 3G

claim: 10.3% of CA1 pyramidal neurons were undergoing apoptosis in the hippocampus of 5-week-old B6J.Gtpbp1-/-; Gcn2-/- mice.
source: Finally, although CA1 pyramidal neurons do not normally degenerate in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice, 10.3% of these neurons were undergoing apoptosis in the hippocampus of 5-week-old B6J.Gtpbp1-/-; Gcn2-/- mice (Figure 3G and H).
evidence: Histological analysis and quantification shown in Figure 3G and 3H

claim: CA1 pyramidal neurons do not normally degenerate in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: Finally, although CA1 pyramidal neurons do not normally degenerate in B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice, 10.3% of these neurons were undergoing apoptosis in the hippocampus of 5-week-old B6J.Gtpbp1-/-; Gcn2-/- mice (Figure 3G and H).
evidence: Observation that CA1 neurons are normally spared in Gtpbp1-/- mice

claim: Neurodegeneration was not observed in the B6J.Gcn2-/- brain.
source: As previously reported (Ishimura et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2002), neurodegeneration was not observed in the B6J.Gcn2-/- brain (data not shown).
evidence: Citation to previous reports and statement of observation

claim: Upstream regulator analysis revealed enrichment of mTOR in differentially expressed genes in the cerebellum of B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice.
source: Upstream regulator analysis of differentially expressed genes in the cerebellum of B6J.Gtpbp1-/- mice (DE Gtpbp1) revealed enrichment, although lower than that observed for ATF4, of the mammalian target of rapamycin kinase (mTOR) (Figure 3A, inset).
evidence: Ingenuity Pathway Analysis results shown in Figure 3A inset

claim: mTOR functions in two distinct protein complexes known as mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1) and complex 2 (mTORC2).
source: mTOR functions in two distinct protein complexes known as mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1) and complex 2 (mTORC2).
evidence: Established knowledge about mTOR complex organization

claim: The central role of mTOR in protein translation is largely attributed to mTORC1 through phosphorylation of specific effector proteins and translation of genes with 5' TOP tracts.
source: Although association with membrane bound ribosomes (i.e. the endoplasmic reticulum) has been observed for mTORC2, the central role of mTOR in protein translation is largely attributed to mTORC1 through phosphorylation of specific effector proteins and translation of particular genes that contain 5' terminal oligopyrimidine (TOP) tracts (Dai and Lu, 2009; Laplante and Sabatini, 2013; Laplante and Sabatini, 2009; Ma and Blenis, 2009a; Ma and Blenis, 2009b; Nandagopal and Roux, 2015; Zinzalla et al., 2011).
evidence: Multiple citations supporting the role of mTORC1 in translation

claim: Only one of 53 detected 5'TOP genes had altered translational efficiency in the B6J.Gtpbp1-/- cerebellum.
source: Only one of the 53 detected 5'TOP genes had an altered TE in the B6J.Gtpbp1-/- cerebellum (Rps29, TE Gtpbp1) or in the B6J-Gtpbp2-/- cerebellum (Rplp0, TE Gtpbp2) compared to the B6J cerebellum (Supplementary file 3, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Translational efficiency analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A

claim: Levels of p-S6240/244 were unchanged at 3 weeks of age in the cerebellum of B6J.Gtpbp1-/- and B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice.
source: In addition, levels of p-S6240/244 were unchanged at 3 weeks of age in the cerebellum of both mutant strains, suggesting that mTOR signaling is not altered by ribosome pausing in granule cells, which comprise the vast majority of cells in the cerebellum (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: Western blot analysis shown in Figure 3B and quantification in Figure 3C

claim: mTOR signaling is not altered by ribosome pausing in cerebellar granule cells.
source: In addition, levels of p-S6240/244 were unchanged at 3 weeks of age in the cerebellum of both mutant strains, suggesting that mTOR signaling is not altered by ribosome pausing in granule cells, which comprise the vast majority of cells in the cerebellum (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: Inference from unchanged p-S6 phosphorylation levels in cerebellum

claim: p-S6240/244 levels were decreased by about 90% in the hippocampus of 3-week-old B6J.Gtpbp1-/- and B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice relative to wild type.
source: In contrast to the cerebellum, p-S6240/244 levels were decreased by about 90% in the hippocampus of 3-week-old B6J.Gtpbp1-/- and B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice relative to wild type (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: Western blot and quantification shown in Figure 3B and 3C

claim: The reduction of p-S6240/244 in the mutant hippocampus was more pronounced in specific neuron populations.
source: Interestingly, immunofluorescence using antibodies to p-S6240/244 revealed that the reduction of p-S6240/244 in the mutant hippocampus was more pronounced in specific neuron populations.
evidence: Immunofluorescence analysis showing cell-type specific differences

claim: In the control hippocampus, p-S6240/244 signal was most intense in CA3 pyramidal cells and lower in CA1 pyramidal cells and DG granule cells.
source: In the control hippocampus, p-S6240/244 signal was most intense in CA3 pyramidal cells and lower in CA1 pyramidal cells and DG granule cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: Immunofluorescence imaging shown in Figure 4A

claim: In B6J.Gtpbp1-/- and B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mutant hippocampi, p-S6240/244 levels were dramatically reduced in the granule cells of the DG and some scattered CA1 neurons.
source: In B6J.Gtpbp1-/- and B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mutant hippocampi, p-S6240/244 levels were dramatically reduced in the granule cells of the DG and some scattered CA1 neurons (Figure 4A).
evidence: Immunofluorescence imaging shown in Figure 4A

claim: Levels of p-S6240/244 were not affected in CA3 neurons of 3-week-old B6J.Gtpbp1-/- and B6J-Gtpbp2-/- mice.

claim: GTPBP1 and GTPBP2 function as ribosome-rescue factors.

claim: The lack of neurodegeneration in mice heterozygous for mutations in both Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 suggests these trGTPases function in the same pathway to mitigate ribosome stalling.
source: In addition, the lack of neurodegeneration in mice heterozygous for mutations in both Gtpbp1 and Gtpbp2 and the lack of an additive phenotype in the brains of mice lacking both genes suggest that these trGTPases function in the same pathway to mitigate ribosome stalling, perhaps mediating different steps in this pathway.

claim: GTPBP1 and GTPBP2 may mediate different steps in the ribosome-rescue pathway.

claim: GTPBP1 and GTPBP2 share domain homology with the yeast protein Hbs1.

claim: Hbs1 and its interacting partner Dom34 recognize paused ribosomes at the 3'end of truncated mRNAs and in the 3'UTR of mRNAs.
source: Hbs1 and its interacting partner Dom34 recognize paused ribosomes at the 3'end of truncated mRNAs and in the 3'UTR of mRNAs, and the resolution of paused ribosomes is in part gated by the GTPase activity of Hbs1 (Becker et al., 2012; Guydosh et al., 2017; Guydosh and Green, 2014; Juszkiewicz et al., 2020; Pisareva et al., 2011; Shoemaker and Green, 2011).

claim: The GTPase activity of GTPBP1 and GTPBP2 is not stimulated in the presence of 80S ribosomes.

claim: GTPBP1 and GTPBP2 likely function differently than Hbs1.

claim: Dom34/Hbs1 did not mediate pause resolution in a codon-specific manner when pausing was induced at His codons upon inhibition of histidine biosynthesis.

claim: GTPBP1 can stimulate exosomal degradation of mRNAs.

claim: GTPBP2 cannot stimulate exosomal degradation of mRNAs.
